params.name: fromDateTime
params.description: Start date and time to get prices for. (Optional, Defaults to "now".)

params.name: toDateTime
params.description: End date and time to get prices for. (Optional, Defaults to fromDateTime plus 3 days.)

params.name: masterTariffId
params.description: You can use this rather than a location (addressString or zipCode) and customer class. We will use the tariffs information to return its price, or in the case of a smart price request, its applicable Smart Tariffs price (Optional)

params.name: zipCode or postCode
params.description: Recommended way to pass a location. Make sure it’s just the ZIP code or post code though. (Optional)

params.name: country
params.description: Use when passing in a postCode or zipCode. Set to the ISO Country Code you require (Optional)

params.name: addressString
params.description: An alternate to using postCode or zipCode and can be an address of any kind. Ideally this will contain a ZIP code or post code. (Optional)

params.name: customerClass
params.description: Denotes the type of customer and is used to determine the appropriate tariff or smart tariff. (Optional) Defaults to "RESIDENTIAL"

params.name: endUse
params.description: Primarily used for smart tariffs. You can use this denote what end use (e.g. appliance, EV, whole home, thermostat etc) the price signal is for. (Optional). You can get the actual values that you can pass in from the property keys residentialEndUse and commercialEndUse

params.name: groupBy
params.description: Use to specify the intervals you want the price changes back in. (Optional) When not passed in you get a change record for each actual change in price. Passing in "HOUR" will give hourly prices, even if the price doesn’t change.

params.name: territoryId
params.description: Rarely needed. This is the for when a tariff has different rates for different territories (so its not for a utility companies service area territory). Only needed when you want to override the default territory. (Optional)

params.name: consumptionAmount
params.description: A monthly consumption in kWh. This is used for banded consumption to determine which pricing to use for the request. By default, the rate amount calculation assumes the highest banded level of consumption. (Optional)

params.name: demandAmount
params.description: A monthly demand in kW. This is used for banded demand to determine which pricing to use for the request. By default, the rate amount calculation assumes the highest banded level of demand. (Optional)

params.description: If specified, all versions of a tariff belonging to the master tariff Id are returned.

params.name: effectiveOn
params.description: Only tariffs that are effective on this date

params.name: openOn
params.description: Only tariffs that were open (i.e. were not closed to new customers) on this date.

params.name: isActive
params.description: Only the current, active tariff version for the LSE or master tariff Id.

params.name: fromDateTime
params.description: Only include tariffs that are effective on or after this date

params.name: toDateTime
params.description: Only include tariffs that are effective on or before this date

params.name: customerClasses
params.description: Comma separated string that indicates the customer classes to include. Choices are: RESIDENTIAL, GENERAL, SPECIAL_USE

params.name: chargeTypes
params.description: Comma separated string that indicates the charge types to include. Choices are: FIXED_PRICE, CONSUMPTION_BASED, DEMAND_BASED, QUANTITY, MINIMUM, TAX, NET_EXCESS_GENERATION

params.name: tariffTypes
params.description: Comma separated string that indicates the tariff types to include. Choices are: DEFAULT, ALTERNATIVE, OPTIONAL_EXTRA, RIDER

params.name: serviceTypes
params.description: Comma separated string that indicates the service types to include. Choices are: ELECTRICITY, SOLAR_PV, ‘GAS’ (default is all serviceTypes)

params.name: privacyFlags
params.description: Comma separated string that indicates the privacy flags types to include. Only applicable if you publish private tariffs. Choices are: PUBLIC, UNLISTED, PRIVATE

params.name: zipCode
params.description: (Optional but Recommended) Use this to return just the Tariffs that are for this given location. Most Tariffs apply for a regional, not national, geography.

params.name: postCode
params.description: Alias for zipCode. You can use either.

params.name: lat
params.description: (Optional) Represents the latitude of a geographical location. This should be paired with lng when not supplying a zip code or address.

params.name: lng
params.description: (Optional) Represents the longitude of a geographical location. This should be paired with lat when not supplying a zip code or address.

params.name: addressString
params.description: An alternative to using zipCode. Use this if you do not have the address parsed out in your app, but instead have a long string. For the best results this string will contain a zipcode or post code. If you do have the address split out it is better to use postCode.

params.name: riderId
params.description: When set to the masterTariffId of a Rider, this will return all of the tariffs that the rider is used on

params.name: populateProperties
params.description: Populates the properties for the returned tariffs

params.name: populateRates
params.description: Populates the rate details for the returned tariffs

params.name: populateDocuments
params.description: Populates the document links for the returned tariffs

params.name: consumption
params.description: Return tariffs which are eligible for this consumption amount

params.name: demand
params.description: Return tariffs which are eligible for this demand amount

params.name: hasNetMetering
params.description: Return tariffs which have or do not have any net metered tariff rates

params.name: hasTimeOfUseRates
params.description: Return tariffs which have or do not have any time-of-use rates

params.name: hasTieredRates
params.description: Return tariffs which have or do not have any tiered rates

params.name: hasContractedRates
params.description: Return tariffs which have or do not have any contracted rates

params.name: bundleRates
params.description: When true (false by default) the rates are summarized (bundled). Note that this only works for tariffs with a customerClass of RESIDENTIAL.

params.name: applicableRatesOnly
params.description: When true (false by default) rate applicability criteria will be applied to the rates. You’ll only get back rates that match the requests rate applicability values, or the default rate applicability value as set on the tariff.

params.name: filterRiderRates
params.description: Used in concert with populateRates = true, when filterRiderRates = true (false by default) rider rates will not be returned. However pointers to the riders will be returned. This is used primarily when using and existing tariff’s structure when creating private tariffs

params.name: filterByApplicability
params.description: applies a rule that results should also be filtered by applicability (i.e., additional eligibility properties).

params.name: applicabilityFilters[solarPvEligible]
params.description: which is the specific applicability criteria to filter by

params.description: ext to return extended fields

params.description: This is from the standard searching and sorting parameters. You can search within one or more of the attributes within the LSE object (see above).

params.name: zipCode
params.description: Zip or post code where you would like to see a list of LSEs for (e.g. 5 digit ZIP code for USA). Most countries have regional, not national, Utility Service Areas. When populating this field you should also populate country too. (Recommended)

params.name: postCode
params.description: Alias for zipCode, you can use either.

params.name: country
params.description: Use an ISO Country Code when passing in a zipCode or postCode, and set it to the ISO Country Code of your zipCode or postCode since some countries use the same format

params.name: ownerships
params.description: Filter results by the type of ownership structure for the LSE. Values include "INVESTOR", "COOP", "MUNI", but see ownership field above for complete list.

params.name: serviceTypes
params.description: Filter results to LSEs that just offer this service type to a customer class. Valid values include "ELECTRICITY" and "SOLAR_PV"

params.name: residentialServiceTypes
params.description: Filter results to LSEs that just offer this service type to their residential customers. Valid values include "ELECTRICITY" and "SOLAR_PV"

params.name: commercialServiceTypes
params.description: Filter results to LSEs that just offer this service type to their commercial (business) customers. Valid values include "ELECTRICITY" and "SOLAR_PV"

params.name: industrialServiceTypes
params.description: Filter results to LSEs that just offer this service type to their industrial customers. Valid values include "ELECTRICITY" and "SOLAR_PV"

params.name: transportationServiceTypes
params.description: Filter results to LSEs that just offer this service type to their transportation customers. Valid values include "ELECTRICITY" and "SOLAR_PV" (Optional).

params.name: zipCode
params.description: The zip code or postal code we will use to look up local buildings.

params.name: country
params.description: The ISO country code. Use in conjunction with zipCode | postCode parameters.

params.name: addressString
params.description: The address string we will geo-tag (isolate latitude & longitude) to look up local buildings.

params.name: lat
params.description: Latitude to look up. Use in concert with lng if you choose this method.

params.name: lng
params.description: Longitude to look up. Use in concert with lat if you choose this method.

params.name: customerClass
params.description: The class of customer, which is one of RESIDENTIAL, GENERAL, or SPECIAL_USE.

params.name: buildingType
params.description: The building type that best describes this building. Use RESIDENTIAL for a residential default or one of the more explicit choices returned from the property key buildingTypeResidential or buildingTypeCommercial.

params.name: serviceType
params.description: This is currently limited to ELECTRICITY.

params.name: buildingArea
params.description: If you have the site footprint, pass in size of the building in square feet. If this is not passed directly we will default to the average for the region and buildingType.

params.name: buildingVintage
params.description: The construction year of the building, options include Pre1980, Post1980 (1980 - 2003), or New (2003+).

params.name: excludeMeasures
params.description: Setting to true will omit the measures (makes the call faster if you don't need this data). Defaults to false.

params.name: measuresUnit
params.description: By default, we will return total usage per interval. If you ask for intensity we'll convert this into energy intensity (e.g. per square foot or meter). Your final choice is proportion which means that each value in the year will add up to 100.

params.name: groupBy
params.description: When supplied the response will roll up measures into this period. Possible values are MONTH, DAY, YEAR.

params.name: sizingKeyName
params.description: Pass this parameter when you want to adjust the size of the load. Currently supports loadSize. Used in concert with sizingDataValue and sizingUnit.

params.name: sizingDataValue
params.description: This should be set to the quantity to size (e.g. 12000 for 12,000 kWh). (See sizingKeyName above)

params.name: sizingUnit
params.description: This denotes the unit of measure for the accompanying sizingDataValue. Currently, we support only kWh. (See sizingKeyName above)

params.name: intervalFromDateTime
params.description: Pass this parameter when you want the "intervals" to be populated from a certain date (e.g. 2024-01-01).

params.name: intervalToDateTime
params.description: Pass this parameter when you want the "intervals" to be populated to a certain date (e.g. 2025-01-01).
